summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi. He was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

Atsushi Uno is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu Universities under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, Dalsukh D. Malvania, Muni Jambūvijaya, and Sukhlal Sanghvi. He held posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima, and Kindai Universities.

Atsuuji Ashikaga (1901–1983) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Doshisha University and under Ryosaburo Sakaki (~1920–1923), later serving as professor at Kyoto University from ~1950 to 1965.
Atsuyoshi Keika works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 1990 and as a professor in 2014.

August Fick (1833–1916) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1852–1856) under Theodor Benfey (~1852–1857), and held posts at Göttingen (~1869–1887) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).

August Friedrich Pott (1802–1887) was a linguist and Indologist who founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin, and was appointed professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1833.

August Johan Bernet Kempers (1906–1992) studied at Leiden University (~1925–1933), working in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was director at Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (~1936–1956) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and University of Amsterdam.

August Leskien (1840–1916) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig (under Georg Curtius), and Jena (under August Schleicher). He held posts at Jena and Göttingen before serving as professor at Leipzig University from ~1870 to 1916.

August Schleicher (1821–1868) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Christian Lassen. He held posts at Bonn, Charles University, and Jena.

August Wilhelm Schlegel (1767–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen (~1786–1791) and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1814). He held posts at Jena (~1796–1801) and Bonn (from 1818), and founded Indische Bibliothek.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director of Aliah University (~1881–1899) and was secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain (1925–2013) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1944–1947) and SOAS (~1952–1954), holding posts at BHU (~1953–1971) and as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1990).

Axel Michaels (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Laxmi Nath Srestha and held posts at the University of Bern (~1992–1996) and Heidelberg University (~1996–2018).

B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Carl Bielefeldt, Geshe Rabten, and others across various institutions. He held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1997–2001) and heads the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.
B. N. Mukherjee (1932–2013) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1950–1956) and later held a post there from ~1975 to 1997.

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956) worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Elphinstone College, Columbia University, University of Bonn, University of London, and LSE. He was an economics professor at Sydenham College (~1918–1920).

Baatr U. Kitinov specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (1908–1994) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), Joint/Deputy Director General at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1953–1965), and professor at Panjab University (~1965–1969).
Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and held a post at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1951), Peking University (~1952–1957), the Institute of Philosophy (~1957), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–1995).
